analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction about foreign transaction fees charged on the Harbourline Travel Card and about how an agent treated him, alleging financial loss (£18.40) and distress/inconvenience, meeting CH-1.
analysis.summary: The customer holds a Harbourline Travel Card, which should not charge foreign transaction fees. He was charged six foreign transaction fees totalling £18.40 in Lisbon. The handler confirmed the account tariff was set up wrongly. When he phoned about it, he waited 50 minutes, and he says the agent was short with him and hung up. He wants the fees refunded and an apology for how he was treated. A recording of the 21/10 call has been requested. The handler noted no vulnerability, but the case does not say the customer was asked about support needs. This looks like a bank error under FEE-6/FEE-2 plus a staff conduct concern, and can stay with the complaints handler.

timeline.event: Customer charged foreign transaction fees in Lisbon on Harbourline Travel Card
Customer phoned about fees, waited 50 minutes, agent reportedly short with him and hung up
Handler confirmed 6 FX fees totalling £18.40 due to wrong tariff set-up; call recording from 21/10 requested

analysis.severity_reason: Financial loss is under £100 (£18.40), which on its own would be Low. However, the complaint includes an allegation about staff conduct (agent short and hung up), which CH-6 classes as Medium.

vulnerability.suggested_support: No indicators found in the case text. Handler recorded 'No vulnerability', but the case does not record that the customer was asked about support needs. Consider asking sensitively per VUL-2.

analysis.routing_reason: None of the ESC-1 triggers apply: there is no fraud, lending, vulnerability referral, systemic issue, legal or media threat. The fee error is a known tariff set-up mistake on one account and does not need technical investigation. The staff conduct element can be handled by the complaints handler. If the tariff fault turns out to affect other Travel Card customers, consider Senior Complaints Review.

policy_citations.quote: Foreign transaction fees are not charged on the Harbourline Travel Card. Any such fee on that card is a bank error and FEE-2 applies.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Six FX fees were charged on the customer's Travel Card, so this is a bank error.

policy_citations.quote: the fee must be refunded in full, together with any interest charged on it, plus a goodwill payment in line with policy RED
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Sets the framework for the handler's decision on the fees; the amount is for an authorised person to decide.
The agent conduct allegation raises severity to Medium despite the loss being under £100.

policy_citations.quote: A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction, oral or written, about the bank's products, services or staff
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer is dissatisfied with the fees and with staff treatment.

policy_citations.quote: Complaints handlers resolve complaints themselves unless one of the following applies
policy_citations.how_it_applies: No escalation trigger applies, so the handler retains the case.

policy_citations.quote: If in doubt, record it as a possible vulnerability and ask the customer, sensitively, whether they need any support.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: No indicators found, but the case does not show the customer was asked.
